mainTopic: The מחלוקת of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about burning the קומץ when the מנחה is missing something, and the source that a קמיצה must be done with the right hand.
overview: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about a מנחה whose שירים went missing before the קומץ was burned. רבי יוחנן says the קומץ is still burned, and ריש לקיש says it is not. First the גמרא clears up a side point in רבי יהושע's ברייתא: the מנחה it mentions is the מנחת נסכים. Then each side reads the פסוק 'מן המנחה' its own way. רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from the לחם הפנים, ריש לקיש's answer fails, and he goes silent. רב אדא בר אהבה learns from that silence that חסרון is like a מום, but רב יוסף בר שמעיה shows the silence proves nothing. רב מלכיו tries to refute רבי יוחנן from two פסוקים about missing offerings. The גמרא answers that the פסוקים only require refilling and forbid eating the missing שירים, which זעירי and רבי ינאי confirm. Finally, the גמרא learns from the four mentions of 'שמאלית' by the מצורע that a קמיצה must be done with the right hand, and רבי ירמיה starts a new question about the word 'right' in that פרשה.

steps.title: Why is a meal offering mentioned in this ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא about sprinkling blood mentions a מנחה at all, since a מנחה has no blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meal offering doing here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask a side question about the ברייתא of רבי יהושע. It mentions a מנחה, but this ברייתא is about sprinkling blood, and a flour offering has no blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that if only a מנחה remains, the blood is not sprinkled. That seems strange, because a regular מנחה has nothing to do with sprinkling blood. So the גמרא wants to know which kind of מנחה the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal offering made of flour
What is it doing here? (Why is it mentioned?)
Sprinkling the blood of an animal offering on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this question is about the main argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. It is a side question that clears up the wording of the ברייתא before the גמרא goes back to that argument.

phrases.english: A meal offering — what is it doing here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about a detail in the ברייתא that רבי יוחנן quoted earlier on the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of מנחה does a ברייתא about sprinkling blood mean?

steps.title: It means the meal offering that comes with libations
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the ברייתא means the מנחת נסכים, the flour offering brought together with an animal offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is talking about the meal offering of libations.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. The ברייתא is not talking about a regular מנחה. It means the מנחת נסכים that comes along with an animal offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחת נסכים is connected to an animal offering, and that offering does have blood. So it makes sense for the ברייתא to ask whether this מנחה is enough to allow sprinkling the animal's blood.

keyTerms.meaning: The flour offering brought along with the wine poured on the מזבח that accompany an animal offering

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The meal offering of libations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא means the מנחת נסכים that comes with an animal offering.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא needed to teach this
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains the mistake the ברייתא is preventing: we might have thought the מנחת נסכים counts as part of the animal itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since it comes together with the animal offering, it is like the offering itself. So the ברייתא teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains why the ברייתא had to say this. Without it, we might have thought that a leftover מנחת נסכים is enough to allow sprinkling the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken thought was that because the מנחת נסכים always comes with the זבח, it counts as part of the זבח. If so, having it left over would be like having some of the animal left over, and the blood could be sprinkled. The ברייתא teaches that this is wrong: it is a separate offering and does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (the reasoning we would have had before this teaching)
So it teaches us (that this thought is wrong)
An animal offering

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of רבי יהושע: a small amount of the animal left over is enough to sprinkle the blood, but a leftover מנחת נסכים is not. This sets up the next question: does a small leftover also count for a regular מנחה?

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say:
since it comes along with an animal offering,
it is like the body of the offering itself,
phrases.notes: He means: if only this מנחה were left, it would count as if part of the animal were left, and we could sprinkle the blood.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב פפא's answer by explaining why the ברייתא needed to say it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is needed so we don't think a מנחת נסכים counts as part of the זבח itself.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a מנחה is different because of a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows how ריש לקיש answers the proof from רבי יהושע: a פסוק teaches that the קומץ is burned only when the whole מנחה is there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who disqualifies — he says it is different here, because the פסוק says: 'And the כהן shall lift from the meal offering its memorial part and burn it on the altar.' 'The meal offering' teaches that until the whole meal offering is there, he may not burn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main argument. It asks how ריש לקיש, who disqualifies the קומץ, deals with the ברייתא, and answers that a מנחה has its own special פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן wanted to learn from a זבח (a small leftover is enough) to a מנחה. ריש לקיש says you cannot compare them. The extra word 'הַמִּנְחָה' in the פסוק teaches that for a מנחה, the קומץ is burned only if the entire מנחה is still there.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who disqualifies (here, ריש לקיש)
It is different here
The 'memorial part', meaning the קומץ that is burned on the מזבח
He shall burn (on the מזבח)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one side can block a proof: it agrees with the ברייתא about a זבח but says a מנחה follows a different rule because of its own פסוק.

phrases.english: And the one who disqualifies —
phrases.notes: This is ריש לקיש, who holds that the קומץ may not be burned if the rest of the מנחה is missing.

phrases.english: it is different here, as the verse says:
"And the priest shall lift from the meal offering
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:9

phrases.english: its memorial part, and shall burn it on the altar";
"the meal offering" —
until the entire meal offering is present,
he shall not burn it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש and explains how ריש לקיש deals with רבי יוחנן's proof from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases through a פסוק (שאני הכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא of רבי יהושע would show that a small leftover is enough for a מנחה too.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מנחה is different: 'הַמִּנְחָה' requires the whole מנחה to be there before the קומץ is burned.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: whole only at the time of קמיצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק differently: the מנחה only has to be whole when the קומץ is taken, and then the קומץ may be burned even if the מנחה is no longer whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one reads 'from the meal offering' as: a meal offering that was already whole at the time of taking the handful, he burns it, even though now it is not whole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוחנן reads the same פסוק. To him it teaches that what matters is the moment the קומץ is taken, not the moment it is burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same פסוק. ריש לקיש says the whole מנחה must be there when the קומץ is burned. רבי יוחנן says it only needs to be whole at the קמיצה, so losing part of it afterward does not stop the burning.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (here, רבי יוחנן)
Taking the handful (the קומץ) out of the מנחה
Whole, complete
Even though

steps.whatToRemember: The argument comes down to timing. ריש לקיש: the מנחה must be whole when the קומץ is burned. רבי יוחנן: it only has to be whole when the קומץ is taken.

phrases.english: And the other one reads "from the meal offering" as:
a meal offering that was already whole
at the time of taking the handful — he shall burn it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּהַשְׁתָּא אֵינָהּ שְׁלֵימָה.
phrases.english: even though now it is not whole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's reading of the same פסוק that ריש לקיש used in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the same פסוק a different meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to require the whole מנחה to be there when the קומץ is burned, which goes against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only requires the מנחה to be whole at the קמיצה. After that, the קומץ is burned even if the rest is no longer whole.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from the shewbread ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes a ברייתא. Once it is time to take the לחם הפנים off the שולחן, the frankincense in the בזיכין is burned even if the bread has broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש from a ברייתא. If the bread broke before it was taken off the table, it is unfit, and the frankincense in the bowls is not burned for it. If the bread broke after it was taken off, the bread is unfit, but the frankincense is still burned for it. רבי אלעזר said: 'taken off' does not mean actually taken off. It means once the time to take it off has come, even if it was not yet taken off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's view that the קומץ is burned only if the whole מנחה is still there. He uses a case about the לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The frankincense in the בזיכין works like the קומץ, and the bread works like the rest of the מנחה. The ברייתא says the frankincense is burned even though the bread is now broken, as long as the bread was whole when its time to be taken off came. That matches רבי יוחנן: wholeness is needed only at the earlier key moment, not at the burning.

keyTerms.meaning: He took it off, meaning the shewbread arrangement taken off the שולחן
Broke into pieces
The bowls of frankincense placed next to the לחם הפנים, burned on the מזבח
Burns on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי אלעזר (אלעזר, the אמורא who explains the ברייתא here) with רבי אליעזר (אליעזר, the תנא whom ריש לקיש brings up in the next step). The names look almost the same.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
If, before he took it off the table, the bread broke,

phrases.aramaic: פָּסוּל, וְאֵין מַקְטִיר עָלָיו אֶת הַבָּזִיכִין,
phrases.english: it is unfit, and he does not burn the bowls of frankincense for it;
and if its bread broke after he took it off,

phrases.aramaic: הַלֶּחֶם פָּסוּל, וּמַקְטִיר עָלָיו אֶת הַבָּזִיכִין.
phrases.english: the bread is unfit, but he burns the bowls of frankincense for it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא פֵּרְקָהּ מַמָּשׁ,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said: not actually taken off,
rather, once its time to be taken off has arrived,
even though he has not taken it off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a ברייתא to back up רבי יוחנן's reading from Step 5 and to attack ריש לקיש's reading from Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that the קומץ is burned only when the whole מנחה is still there.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The frankincense is burned even though the bread is broken. So burning does not need the rest of the offering to be whole at that moment.

steps.title: ריש לקיש says the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, whom he does not follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: Whose view is this? It is רבי אליעזר's.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends himself. He says the ברייתא matches the view of רבי אליעזר, not the view he follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that the קומץ is burned even if the rest of the מנחה is gone. ריש לקיש follows רבי יהושע, so a ברייתא that agrees with רבי אליעזר does not bind him.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? A way of tying a source to one particular opinion

phrases.english: He said to him: Whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Eliezer's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to one side of a מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be the accepted halacha, against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only reflects רבי אליעזר's view, and ריש לקיש follows רבי יהושע.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: this is an unattributed teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן objects that the ברייתא is stated without any name. It should not be pushed off as one תנא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am telling you a complete teaching, and you tell me it is רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects ריש לקיש's answer. A ruling taught with no name attached should not be written off as one person's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling taught without a name usually reflects the accepted, mainstream view. Tying it to רבי אליעזר alone weakens its authority, and רבי יוחנן finds that hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: A complete teaching, meaning a ruling taught with no name and no stated disagreement

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא אָמֵינָא לָךְ מִשְׁנָה שְׁלֵימָה,
phrases.english: He said to him: I am telling you a complete teaching,
phrases.notes: He means a ruling taught plainly, with no name on it, so it sounds like everyone agrees.

phrases.english: and you tell me it is Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: ריש לקיש's attempt to tie the ברייתא to רבי אליעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ruling taught with no name should not be pushed off as one תנא's minority view.

steps.title: Why say 'broke' if רבי אליעזר allows even total loss?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds a second problem. If the ברייתא were רבי אליעזר's, it should not depend on the bread being broken. ריש לקיש goes silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי אליעזר, why mention specifically 'broke'? Even if the bread were burned or lost, he would allow it! ריש לקיש was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן shows that the ברייתא's wording does not fit רבי אליעזר. ריש לקיש has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר allows burning even when the rest of the offering is completely gone. So a ברייתא following him would not bother with the smaller case of bread that only broke. ריש לקיש has no reply.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? Used to ask why a source picks a narrow case
Burned and lost, meaning completely gone
He rules it fit
He was silent, meaning he had no answer

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, מַאי אִירְיָא נִפְרַס?
phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Eliezer, why specifically 'broke'?
Even if burned or lost, he would also rule it fit!
He was silent.
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is the one who goes quiet. He has no reply.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, מַאי אִירְיָא נִפְרַס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, stronger attack on ריש לקיש's answer from Step 7. The exchange ends with his silence.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the ברייתא to רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's narrow case ('broke') makes no sense under רבי אליעזר's broad leniency, since he would allow it even if the bread were burned or lost.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's attempt to tie the ברייתא to רבי אליעזר fails on two counts: the ruling has no name on it, and its wording does not fit רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Why didn't ריש לקיש say communal offerings are different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש stayed silent. He could have answered that the לחם הפנים is a communal offering, and communal offerings get special leniencies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why was he silent? Let him answer: the community is different. Since טומאה was allowed for them, missing parts should also be allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and asks why ריש לקיש did not use an obvious answer. This sets up the next step, which explains why that answer would not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communal offerings may be brought even in טומאה. So one might think a communal offering like the לחם הפנים can also be brought when it is missing a piece. That would mean the ברייתא says nothing about a private מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: The community is different. Communal offerings have their own rules
Ritual impurity
Was permitted
Offerings that are missing part of their measure

phrases.english: But why was he silent? Let him say to him:
the community is different,
since impurity was permitted for them,
missing offerings were also permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the silence at the end of Step 9 by offering a possible defense.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why ריש לקיש did not answer that communal offerings are allowed even when missing a piece.

steps.title: A missing piece counts like a blemish
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that ריש לקיש's silence shows a missing piece counts like a מום, and a מום is never allowed, even for the ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: This shows that being short is like having a blemish, and a blemished offering is not allowed even for the community.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה answers the question from Step 10. He learns a rule from the fact that ריש לקיש did not use the 'ציבור is different' answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציבור's leniency covers טומאה, not a מום. Missing part of an offering is like a physical flaw in the offering itself, so it falls under the stricter category of מום. That is why the communal exception could not help ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: This shows, meaning we can learn a rule from what just happened
Being short or missing part
An offering with a blemish, which is disqualified

steps.whyThisMatters: It proposes a general rule: a missing part counts like a blemish, not like impurity. So even communal offerings, which may be brought in טומאה, could not be brought when something is missing. The next step challenges whether ריש לקיש's silence really proves this.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אדא בר אהבה learns from ריש לקיש's silence that חסרון is treated like a מום, and the ציבור's leniency for טומאה does not cover a מום. The next step challenges whether the silence really proves this.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת,
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said: This is to say,
being short is considered like a blemished animal,
and there is no blemished offering for the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Communal leniency covers טומאה but not a מום, and חסרון counts as a מום, so the answer would not have worked.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אדא בר אהבה infers from the silence that חסרון counts like a מום, which is never allowed, even for communal offerings. Step 12 challenges this inference.

steps.title: The silence proves nothing, because the omer offering is also communal
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר שמעיה challenges רב אדא בר אהבה's inference. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree even about the מנחת העומר, which is a communal offering. So the 'communal offering' answer was never open to ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא was sitting and repeating this teaching. רב יוסף בר שמעיה said to רב פפא: Aren't רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש arguing even about the מנחת העומר, which is a communal offering? And they still disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא repeats רב אדא בר אהבה's lesson from step 11. רב יוסף בר שמעיה pushes back and says the lesson does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא learned from ריש לקיש's silence that he could have said 'communal offerings are different' but chose not to. רב יוסף points out that the argument covers the מנחת העומר, which is already communal, so that answer was never available. That means the silence teaches us nothing about a missing piece counting like a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or halachic discussion
We are dealing with (this case)
The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן, which is a communal offering
They disagree

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not arguing about whether a מום is allowed for the ציבור. He only shows that ריש לקיש's silence cannot be used as evidence, because the 'communal' answer did not fit the case they were arguing about.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the source for the idea that a missing amount in a מנחה is like a מום.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב פָּפָּא וְקָאָמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa was sitting and saying this teaching,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר שְׁמַעְיָה לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Shemaya said to Rav Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: Aren't we dealing with the dispute of Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish
even in the omer offering, which is communal, and still they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference made in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's inference that a missing amount counts like a מום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מחלוקת includes the מנחת העומר, which is communal. So ריש לקיש could not have answered 'communal offerings are different,' and his silence proves nothing.

steps.title: First ברייתא: missing any flour or oil disqualifies the meal offering
steps.stepSummary: רב מלכיו quotes a ברייתא. From the words 'of its flour' and 'of its oil' it learns that a מנחה missing even a tiny amount of either one is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מלכיו said: One ברייתא teaches: 'Of its flour' teaches that if it is missing any amount at all, it is disqualified. 'Of its oil' teaches that if it is missing any amount at all, it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מלכיו starts a new line of discussion about the same מחלוקת by quoting a first ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'its' in 'its flour' and 'its oil' means the full, complete amount. So if even a little flour or oil is missing, the כהן may not take the קומץ from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine flour
Oil
Any amount at all, even the smallest bit
Disqualified

phrases.english: Rav Malkiyu said: One baraita teaches:
"Of its flour": that if it is missing any amount, it is disqualified;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:2

phrases.english: "Of its oil": that if it is missing any amount, it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new approach to the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנחה missing any amount of its flour or oil is פסול.

steps.title: Second ברייתא: 'what is left of the meal offering' rules out missing offerings
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא learns from 'and what is left of the מנחה' that the כהנים get the leftovers only from a complete offering. It rules out a מנחה that was missing, one whose קומץ was missing, and one where no לבונה was burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'And what is left of the מנחה' comes to exclude a מנחה that was missing, one whose קומץ was missing, and one where the כהן burned none of its לבונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מלכיו brings a second ברייתא that also deals with a מנחה that is missing something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'What is left' only makes sense when there was a full offering to begin with. So in these missing cases the offering is פסול and the כהנים may not eat what remains.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is left (the leftovers)
To exclude
The handful taken from the מנחה and burned on the מזבח
Frankincense

phrases.english: And another baraita teaches:
"And what is left of the meal offering":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:3

phrases.english: to exclude a meal offering that was itself missing,
and one whose handful was missing,
and one from whose frankincense he burned nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second source placed next to the first one
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנחה that was missing, or whose קומץ was missing, or where no לבונה was burned, is excluded, and its leftovers are not eaten.

steps.title: Why two verses? One for before the handful is taken, one for after
steps.stepSummary: רב מלכיו asks why two פסוקים are needed to rule out a missing מנחה. He suggests that one covers a מנחה missing before the קמיצה, and the other covers leftovers that went missing between the קמיצה and the הקטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need two פסוקים about missing offerings? Isn't it that one is for a מנחה that became missing before the קמיצה, and one is for leftovers that became missing between the קמיצה and the הקטרה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב מלכיו notices that two פסוקים seem to teach the same thing. He gives each one its own job, setting up a point the גמרא is about to make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second פסוק must teach something new. So it is read as covering the in-between stage, after the קומץ was taken but before it was burned. That stage is exactly what רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about. The next step spells out what follows from this: a challenge to רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking the handful from the מנחה
Burning the handful on the מזבח
The leftovers of the מנחה after the קומץ is taken
Why do I need it? (asking about something that seems extra)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two stages. The first is a מנחה missing before the handful is taken. The second is leftovers that went missing after the handful was taken but before it was burned.

phrases.english: Why do I need two verses about missing offerings?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו חַד לְמִנְחָה שֶׁחָסְרָה קוֹדֶם קְמִיצָה,
phrases.english: Isn't it that one is for a meal offering that became missing before the handful was taken,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד לְשִׁירַיִם שֶׁחָסְרוּ בֵּין קְמִיצָה לְהַקְטָרָה,
phrases.english: and one is for leftovers that became missing between taking the handful and burning it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two ברייתות from steps 13 and 14 and asks why both are needed
steps.raayaObject: Leftovers that went missing between the קמיצה and the הקטרה are disqualified (the stage under dispute)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra פסוק 'והנותרת מן המנחה', next to 'מסלתה' and 'משמנה'

steps.title: Does this refute רבי יוחנן on both points?
steps.stepSummary: רב מלכיו draws the conclusion of his reading: רבי יוחנן seems refuted in both of his disagreements with ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if so, is this a full refutation of רבי יוחנן in both cases?
steps.whatsHappening: רב מלכיו spells out where his reading of the two פסוקים leads. If the פסוקים rule out both cases, then רבי יוחנן is wrong on both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן allows refilling a מנחה that went missing before the קמיצה. He also allows burning the קומץ when the leftovers went missing afterward. If each פסוק disqualifies one of these cases, both of his rulings fall.

keyTerms.meaning: A full refutation, meaning a challenge that knocks down an opinion
In both of them (both cases)

phrases.english: And is it a refutation of רבי יוחנן in both of them?
phrases.notes: "Both" means the two cases from the last step: missing before the קמיצה, and missing between the קמיצה and the burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenging conclusion from רב מלכיו's suggestion in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's two rulings: refilling a missing מנחה, and burning the קומץ for leftovers that went missing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one פסוק disqualifies each case, both of רבי יוחנן's lenient rulings go against the פסוקים.

steps.title: The פסוקים teach refilling and a ban on eating, not full disqualification
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. One פסוק teaches that a missing מנחה is fine only if it is refilled. The other teaches that the קומץ is burned, but the missing leftovers may not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. One פסוק is about a מנחה that went missing before the קמיצה: if he brings flour from home and fills it up, yes, it is fine, and if not, no. The other פסוק is about leftovers that went missing between the קמיצה and the burning: even though he burns the קומץ for them, those leftovers may not be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. It reads both פסוקים in a way that fits רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים are about the same two cases, but they do not throw the offering out. The first only says the מנחה must be filled back up, which is exactly what רבי יוחנן allows. The second only bans eating the leftovers, while burning the קומץ, as רבי יוחנן holds, is still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן takes a fistful of the מנחה to burn on the מזבח
The fistful taken from the מנחה
Burning the קומץ on the מזבח
The leftovers of the מנחה, which the כהנים eat
From his house, meaning from his own extra flour

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the קומץ is disqualified here. According to רבי יוחנן the קומץ is still burned; only eating the missing leftovers is forbidden.

phrases.english: No, one is for a מנחה
that became lacking before the קמיצה,
that if he brings from his house and fills it, yes,
and if not, no,
and one is for leftovers that became lacking
between the קמיצה and the burning,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּמַקְטִיר קוֹמֶץ עֲלֵיהֶן –
phrases.english: that even though he burns the קומץ for them,
those leftovers are forbidden to be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, חַד לְמִנְחָה שֶׁחָסְרָה קוֹדֶם קְמִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation in step 16 by giving each פסוק a milder meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of what each פסוק teaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים fully disqualify both cases, against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first פסוק requires refilling, and the second bans only eating the leftovers. Both fit רבי יוחנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps רבי יוחנן's view standing and separates two things: whether the קומץ may be burned, and whether the leftovers may be eaten.

steps.title: The known question: may leftovers that went missing be eaten?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer with a question the חכמים once raised. For the one who allows burning the קומץ, may the missing leftovers be eaten?
steps.simpleTranslation: For it was asked: according to the one who says that when leftovers went missing between the קמיצה and the burning, he burns the קומץ for them, what is the law about eating those leftovers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a known question to show that 'burn the קומץ, but don't eat the leftovers' is a real position. It is setting up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes the קומץ may be burned, which is רבי יוחנן's view. It asks only about eating. That is exactly the split the גמרא just used to explain the second פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the חכמים)
He burns, here meaning the כהן burns the קומץ
Eating

phrases.english: For it was asked before them:
According to the one who says that leftovers that became lacking
phrases.notes: "The one who says" is רבי יוחנן's view from the earlier argument with ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: between the קמיצה and the burning
he burns the קומץ for them,
those leftovers, what are they regarding eating?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 17 by showing the חכמים discussed eating such leftovers as its own question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether leftovers that went missing between the קמיצה and the burning may be eaten, once the קומץ is burned for them.

steps.title: זעירי and רבי ינאי: the missing leftovers may not be eaten
steps.stepSummary: Both answer from the פסוק that the leftovers may not be eaten. זעירי learns it from 'and what is left,' and רבי ינאי learns it from 'of the מנחה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: the פסוק says 'and what is left,' and not what is left of what is left. רבי ינאי said: 'of the מנחה' means a מנחה that already existed whole.
steps.whatsHappening: Two חכמים answer the question. Each uses a different word in the פסוק to show that the missing leftovers may not be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי reads 'what is left' as the leftovers of a whole מנחה. Leftovers that later lost some more are 'left of what is left,' so they are not included. רבי ינאי reads 'of the מנחה' as requiring a מנחה that was complete. This confirms step 17: the קומץ is burned, but the leftovers are not eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And what is left,' meaning the leftovers given to the כהנים
What is left of what is left: leftovers that lost even more
A מנחה that already existed whole

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, if leftovers go missing after the קמיצה, the קומץ is still burned, but those leftovers may not be eaten. זעירי learns this from 'והנותרת' and רבי ינאי from 'מהמנחה.'

phrases.english: זעירי said: the verse says, 'and what is left,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:3

phrases.english: and not what is left of what is left.
And רבי ינאי said:
'Of the מנחה': a מנחה that already was.
phrases.notes: He means a מנחה that was still whole, before anything went missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18, which confirms the reading given in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The leftovers may not be eaten. זעירי learns it from 'והנותרת' (not what is left of what is left), and רבי ינאי from 'מהמנחה' (a מנחה that was whole).

steps.title: What is the source that a left-hand קמיצה is invalid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a קמיצה done with the left hand and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that if the כהן took the handful with his left hand, it is פסול. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה and asks where the rule comes from. This sets up רבי זירא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed a קמיצה done with the left hand as פסול. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק shows that the קמיצה must be done with the right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Took the קוֹמֶץ, the handful of flour taken from a מִנְחָה to be burned on the מִזְבֵּחַ
Left (hand)
From where are these things learned? A request for a source

phrases.english: If he took the handful with the left hand:
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, which says such a מנחה is פסול.

phrases.english: From where are these matters learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The earlier discussion of a missing מנחה is finished, and the גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that requires the קמיצה to be done with the right hand.

steps.title: רבי זירא: a plain 'כף' always means the right hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא learns that the קמיצה needs the right hand. The Torah says 'כפו' (his hand) for the מנחה, and with the מצורע it had to say 'left' outright. So a plain 'כף' means the right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: the פסוק says 'he brought the מנחה and filled his hand from it.' On its own, I would not know which hand is meant. But with the מצורע the Torah says 'the כהן's left hand.' So there, it is the left. Everywhere else that just says 'hand' means the right hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question. The word 'כף' in the פסוק about the מנחה means the right hand, and he proves it from the פסוק about the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah had to spell out 'left' for the oil of the מצורע. That shows that 'כף' on its own does not mean the left. So any place where the Torah just says 'כף', such as the קמיצה, means the right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Hand or palm
The לוֹג (a measure) of oil brought by a מְצוֹרָע for his purification
The left one (hand)
Right (hand)

steps.confusionAlert: 'כאן שמאלית' does not mean the left hand is used for the קמיצה. It means only here, by the מצורע, is the left hand used. Everywhere else, a plain 'כף' means the right.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: because the verse says:
"And he brought the meal offering
and he filled his hand from it":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 9:17

phrases.english: this 'hand', I do not know which it is,
but when it says: "And the priest shall take from the log of oil
and pour it on the priest's left hand":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:15, about the מצורע's purification.

phrases.english: here it is the left,
which shows that every place where 'hand' is said
means only the right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A plain 'כף' means the right hand. This is learned from the fact that the Torah has to write 'שמאלית' when it means the left, by the מצורע.

steps.title: That word 'left' is needed for its own law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. The word 'שמאלית' by the מצורע is needed to teach that the oil goes on the left hand, so it cannot also teach a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that פסוק is needed for its own purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's proof. The word 'left' by the מצורע is busy teaching the law of the מצורע itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a word in the Torah is needed for its own law, we cannot use it to learn something extra. Here, 'שמאלית' is needed to tell us which hand gets the oil. So it seems it cannot also teach that 'כף' everywhere else means the right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for itself, to teach its own law, so it is not free to teach something else

phrases.english: But isn't it needed for itself?
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק is needed to teach that the מצורע's oil is poured on the left hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof that רבי זירא brought in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's use of 'שמאלית' by the מצורע as a general rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is already needed to teach the מצורע's own law, so it is not free to teach anything more.

steps.title: There is another 'left' in the פרשה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'שמאלית' is written a second time. The first teaches the מצורע's law, and the extra one teaches the general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another 'left' is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי זירא. The word 'left' appears again in the same פרשה, so there is an extra word to learn from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One 'שמאלית' teaches the מצורע's own law. The second, extra 'שמאלית' is free, and it teaches that a plain 'כף' everywhere else means the right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Another one is written, an extra word in the פסוק

phrases.english: Another 'left' is written.
phrases.notes: See ויקרא 14:16, right after the first one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one 'שמאלית' is written, and it is used up by the מצורע's law.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a second 'שמאלית', which is free to teach that a plain 'כף' means the right hand.

steps.title: Two limitations in a row should widen the law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: two 'only left' wordings in a row should follow the rule that one limitation after another comes to include, so the right hand would also be allowed for the מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us say: a limitation after a limitation comes only to include.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the second 'left'. There is a known rule that two limitations in a row actually widen the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each 'שמאלית' limits the law to the left hand. By the rule of אין מיעוט אחר מיעוט אלא לרבות, two limitations in a row cancel out and include. So the right hand would also be allowed for the מצורע, and the extra word could not teach the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A limitation, a word in the Torah that narrows a law

keyTerms.term: אֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת
keyTerms.meaning: A limitation after a limitation comes only to include, so two limitations widen the law

phrases.english: But say: there is no limitation after a limitation
except to include?
phrases.notes: He means that two 'only left' words in a row would allow the right hand for the מצורע too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: אֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 23, which relied on a second 'שמאלית'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of the second 'שמאלית' as a free, extra word
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two limitations in a row widen the law, so the second word would include the right hand instead of teaching a general rule.

steps.title: A third 'left': only here is it the left hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that yet another 'שמאלית' is written. With it, the left hand is required for the מצורע, and it teaches that no other place uses the left.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another 'left' is written. Here it is the left, and nowhere else is it the left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with yet another 'left' in the פרשה. This extra word removes the 'two limitations' problem and teaches that only the מצורע uses the left hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one more 'שמאלית', the words are no longer just 'two limitations in a row', so the left hand stays required for the מצורע. The extra word now teaches that the left hand is used only here, and so 'כף' elsewhere means the right.

keyTerms.meaning: And no other place uses the left hand

phrases.english: Another 'left' is written.
phrases.notes: This is yet another one, in the part about the poor מצורע (ויקרא 14:26).

phrases.english: Here it is the left, and no other is the left.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״שְׂמָאלִית״ אַחֲרִינָא כְּתִיב. כָּאן שְׂמָאלִית, וְאֵין אַחֵר שְׂמָאלִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an additional extra word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two 'left' words are two limitations in a row and so include the right hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: A further 'שמאלית' keeps the left hand required for the מצורע and teaches that no other place uses the left.

steps.title: Maybe the opposite: the left hand everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the extra word could teach the opposite: just as the מצורע uses the left hand, so does every other place.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the opposite: just as here it is the left, so too everywhere else it is the left!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the direction of the lesson. Why should the extra word teach 'only here is it the left'? Maybe it teaches that the left is used everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra word could make the מצורע a model for other cases, which would make the left hand the rule everywhere. That would destroy רבי זירא's proof that a plain 'כף' means the right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary, the exact opposite
In general, everywhere else

phrases.english: But say: on the contrary,
just as here it is the left,
so too generally it is also the left!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 25 by turning its lesson upside down.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'כאן שמאלית ואין אחר שמאלית'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra word could just as well extend the left hand to all cases instead of limiting it to the מצורע.

steps.title: Four times 'left': two for the poor, two for the rich
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'שמאלית' is written four times, two for a poor מצורע and two for a rich one. All these extra words show that the left hand belongs to the מצורע alone, so 'כף' elsewhere means the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four 'left's are written: two about a poor person and two about a rich person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer by counting all the times 'left' appears in the פרשה of the מצורע. There are four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three of the mentions are used to require the left hand for the מצורע and to get past the 'two limitations' problem. The fourth teaches that the left hand is limited to the מצורע alone. So the proof of רבי זירא stands: a plain 'כף', as in the קמיצה, means the right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: A poor person, here a poor מְצוֹרָע who brings a smaller קָרְבָּן
A rich person, here a wealthy מְצוֹרָע

steps.whatToRemember: A קמיצה must be done with the right hand. The Torah says 'כף', and a plain 'כף' means the right hand. We know this because the Torah repeats 'שמאלית' four times by the מצורע, which shows that the left hand is the exception, used only there.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the משנה makes a left-hand קמיצה פסול. It also sets a general rule: wherever the Torah says 'כף' for an עבודה, it means the right hand.

phrases.english: Four 'left's are written:
two about the poor person, and two about the rich person.
phrases.notes: Rich: ויקרא 14:15–16. Poor: ויקרא 14:26–27.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 26 and secures רבי זירא's source from step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counts all the mentions of the word in the פרשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra 'שמאלית' might extend the left hand to every place.
steps.terutzMaskana: With four mentions, the extra one limits the left hand to the מצורע alone. So a plain 'כף' means the right hand, and a left-hand קמיצה is פסול.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'right' for the rich מצורע's oil?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא why the פסוק about putting oil on a rich מצורע needs to say 'right thumb' and 'right big toe.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: The פסוק 'Upon the thumb of his right hand and upon the big toe of his right foot,' written about the oil of a rich מצורע, why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה points to another wording in the מצורע section that seems extra and asks what it comes to teach. This question opens a new round, and the answer will come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's method has been that extra words in the מצורע section each teach something, as with the repeated 'שמאלית.' רבי ירמיה tests that method: if every extra word teaches something, then the word 'right' in the oil פסוק for a rich מצורע also needs a reason. As far as this text shows, the question is simply what the word 'right' adds there.

keyTerms.meaning: Thumb (on the hand) or big toe (on the foot)
The right one (right hand or right foot)
A rich מצורע, who brings the full set of offerings when he becomes pure
'Why do I need it?' The גמרא asks this when a word or פסוק seems to add nothing new

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the oil goes on the right side. Everyone agrees it does. The question is only why the פסוק needs to spell it out.
